text:
pagerbot: [PAGE] us-east-1-pool-9 Dedicated pool reporting steady 5xx+queueing. autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool max_nodes. severity:high :rotating_light:

Dana (oncall): noticed cascading 502s for several tenants, p95 at 2.6s, queue depth x3. Dashboard shows "scale decision: would_add=4 but max_nodes=32 reached".

Lee (sre): confirmed. This is a capacity ceiling issue, not cooldown. Incoming rate ~3.7x normal; looks like an integration partner (quickpay) opened many streams. GPU utilization 96%, KV cache thrashing.

Marco (infra): checking pool config. us-east-1-pool-9 max_nodes=32 (hard limit from dedicated contract). We have warm standby region us-east-1-aux with spare capacity but introducing cross-pool routing needs policy approval.

Dana (oncall): customer-impact: three enterprise customers (fastship, quickpay, medai) are on the pool. fastship and medai are SLA customers — protect them. Quickpay is the noisy one. CS pinged.

Renee (cs): quickpay says they started a mass import and didn't realize it would fan out. They can pause but need 7 minutes to stop. fastship already reported timeouts and is asking for ETA.

Lee (sre): mitigation plan options: A) enable "overcommit_burst" toggle for pool to temporarily exceed max_nodes for 10m (bypasses contract cap but allowed by infra emergency policy) B) apply per-tenant emergency throttle on quickpay C) migrate some SLA tenants to aux pool D) route best-effort traffic to aux pool E) reduce per-connection keepalive to free sockets.

Ivy (eng-runtime): I can do the overcommit toggle and traffic-split. Admin API endpoints: `POST /admin/pools/{pool}/flags { "overcommit_burst": "enable", "ttl_seconds": 600 }` and `PATCH /admin/traffic-shaper` for split rules. Note: overcommit requires 2 approvals because it can breach contractual node caps.

Marco (infra): aux pool us-east-1-aux has ~28% spare capacity. It's slightly older hardware; p95 delta ~250ms if we move heavy inference. We can take SLA tenants temporarily if they accept small latency bump.

Dana (oncall): priority: keep fastship and medai healthy. Plan: 1) apply emergency throttle to quickpay (cap connections / rps) 2) request two approvals to enable overcommit_burst for 10m 3) shift non-SLA and best-effort to aux pool (30%) 4) if errors persist, migrate medai to aux temporarily.

Lee (sre): applying throttle on quickpay now: `POST /admin/quotas` body `{ "tenant_id": "quickpay", "rps_limit": 200, "ttl_seconds": 420 }`

Lee (sre): quota service replied 200. quickpay now capped. Connections dropping by ~45% within 30s.

Renee (cs): quickpay acknowledged and will pause imports in ~5m. fastship says they need status updates every 10m.

Ivy (eng-runtime): requesting approvals to enable overcommit_burst (10m TTL). Opsbot: microsvc policy requires 2 approvers for contract cap overrides. Approvers available? Marco and Lee are ops approvers.

Marco (infra): approving. opsbot: approval logged by marco (infra).

Lee (sre): approving. opsbot: approval logged by lee (sre).

Ivy (eng-runtime): enabling overcommit now: ```curl -X POST "https://admin-api.internal/pools/us-east-1-pool-9/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"overcommit_burst":"enable","ttl_seconds":600}' -v```

Ivy (eng-runtime): admin-api responded 202 Accepted. Orchestration kicked off. opsbot: audit event created. Cost estimate: temporary node overspend ~22% hourly for duration. Posting to #cost-alerts.

Marco (infra): overcommit reported nodes initializing. Expected new nodes in ~100s. Monitoring.

Dana (oncall): meanwhile apply traffic-split for best-effort: push 30% of non-SLA to aux pool. Ivy, can you apply the split?

Ivy (eng-runtime): applied traffic-shaper change: split non-SLA 70/30 to us-east-1-pool-9/us-east-1-aux. Change id fflag-overcommit-1111. opsbot: logged.

Lee (sre): metrics after changes: queue depth halved, p95 down to 1.2s, errors falling to 0.8%. quickpay still high but within new cap.

Renee (cs): fastship says latency improved; they're monitoring. Quickpay paused imports and thanks for the heads up.

Dana (oncall): autoscaler note: because we overcommitted, controller now shows pool nodes=36 (4 over max). We'll monitor contract team notification.

Marco (infra): contract ops notified automatically by opsbot due to cap breach; they acknowledged and will follow up. Recording in incident ticket.

Ivy (eng-runtime): cost notice: enabling overcommit_burst increases billing and triggers chargeback. Logged to cost channel.

Lee (sre): handoff: my shift ends in 8m. I'll monitor for 20m and then start rollback if stable. If errors <0.5% for 15m, we plan to remove overcommit and revert traffic-shaper.

Dana (oncall): patch note for rollback commands stored in incident ticket. Also, note to CS: inform SLA customers when we revert so they can validate.

opsbot: Incident status=mitigated. responders=[dana (oncall), lee (sre), marco (infra), ivy (eng-runtime), renee (cs)]. severity downgraded to medium.

Lee (sre): update at +14m: errors steady at 0.3%, p95 ~1.0s. Overcommit TTL approaching 90s. Initiating graceful scale-down: `POST /admin/pools/us-east-1-pool-9/flags` body `{"overcommit_burst":"disable"}`

Ivy (eng-runtime): disable acknowledged 200. Orchestration draining 4 overcommit nodes. Note: will wait until inflight requests < threshold to terminate.

Marco (infra): drain completed, nodes removed; pool now back to max_nodes=32 at 14:22 UTC. No orphaned VMs observed.

Dana (oncall): reverting traffic-shaper and quotas: removed quickpay cap, reverted split to original. Commands executed and opsbot logged changes.

Renee (cs): customers confirmed stable; fastship signed off. Quickpay confirmed their import is paused.

Lee (sre): closing notes: root cause = unannounced high-volume import from non-SLA tenant fan-out plus pool max_nodes constraint. Actions: temporary throttle, overcommit_burst with approvals, traffic-split to aux pool, communicated to contract ops and customers.

Ivy (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add automated detection for tenant-led fan-outs that preemptively apply soft backpressure, 2) create a safe overcommit workflow to avoid manual approvals when impact is contained, 3) add telemetry to show max_nodes headroom in the console.

Marco (infra): follow-ups: review contract max_nodes thresholds; consider configurable burst quota in contract terms.

Dana (oncall): postmortem assigned to lee+marco+ivy. Handing off monitoring to lee. Good work team. :thumbsup:

opsbot: Incident closed at 14:45 UTC. Postmortem due in 72h.
